solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Playground mat is a basic shape

parts.note: REC is short for recreation ground, a British public playground or park
a mat of hair or fibres is a tangle

explanation.surface: A soft mat in a children's playground is cut to a simple geometric form.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'rec' is the everyday British word for a recreation ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-sided figure with right angles is one of the elementary geometric figures taught first.

clue.text: Hard to manipulate the unconscious mind

parts.note: to rig a result is to manipulate it dishonestly
the id is Freud's name for the unconscious, instinctive part of the psyche

explanation.surface: The unconscious mind is difficult to control.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff and unbending material is firm, not yielding to pressure.

clue.text: Fun putting mad record up loud

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: A noisy party plays a mad record at full volume, all good fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is the golf stroke, not 'placing'; 'up' turns LOG into GOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature golf game with whimsical obstacles is a leisure pastime of putting the ball.

clue.text: Experienced sailors head off charts, each taking on crew

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which comes off

parts.note: charts of figures are tables
the crew of a ship are its men

explanation.surface: Seasoned seafarers lead the way past the charts, each one taking on a crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the first letter of TABLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating qualified for full seamanship duties in the merchant navy or Royal Navy is a trained mariner.

clue.text: Protest ultimately ending with street fight

indicators.note: ultimately, meaning in the end, picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: a rumble is slang for a street fight between gangs

explanation.surface: A demonstration eventually ends in a brawl in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain or grouse is to object, voicing discontent.

clue.text: Court pursues former lover over money that's gone forever

indicators.note: one piece pursuing others comes after them

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A court chases an ex-partner over cash that has vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pursues' means coming after; 'over' is just a link in this down clue. 'Tin' as money is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A species or thing that has died out entirely no longer exists anywhere.

clue.text: Finally getting detailed map of the world

indicators.note: read as de-tailed: the final letter is chopped off the phrase

parts.note: 'at last' is a phrase meaning finally, eventually

explanation.surface: At last you get a detailed world map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' looks like a description of the map but means 'de-tailed': AT LAST loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound book of maps showing the countries of the globe is what one consults for world geography.

clue.text: Once more in decline, leader drops to last place

indicators.note: the leading letter falls from first position to the end

parts.note: to wane is to decline or diminish

explanation.surface: A sports leader slides from the top of the table to the bottom yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader drops to last place' moves the W of WANE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something afresh means starting again, a second time.

clue.text: Take a breather before final decisive strike

parts.note: a lung is literally a breathing organ

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fencer pauses to rest before a final decisive thrust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest, but it is the organ that breathes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden forward thrust, as with a sword, is an attacking blow.

clue.text: Ponder overnight and see point student laboured

indicators.note: laboured letters are worked over, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A student works hard to grasp a point and decides to think about it until morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Delaying a decision until the next day is to let a night's rest help one think.

clue.text: Discovered in Agra — illustrious vessel

indicators.note: something discovered in a stretch of text is found sitting within those words

explanation.surface: A famous cup unearthed in the Indian city of Agra.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'aGRA ILlustrious'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy cup of Arthurian legend is a drinking vessel, the chalice of the Last Supper.

clue.text: Set a higher standard at university, you once devoured advanced books

parts.note: being 'up' is the British idiom for being in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

indicators.note: something devoured is swallowed up inside the eater

parts.note: thee is the old, archaic form of you
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A student at college was once so hungry for knowledge that they consumed advanced textbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoured' signals the archaic pronoun swallowing the other pieces; 'up' for being at Oxford or Cambridge is a British idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the stakes in poker, hence demanding more, is an idiom for pushing expectations higher.

clue.text: Boring Saab's restored and working with new interior, free of moisture!

parts.note: something dull or boring is dry

indicators.note: a restored car has been rebuilt, so the letters of the make are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the car make Saab, the 's being a link (Saab is restored)
a machine that is working is on

indicators.note: the interior of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A dull old Saab gets a refurbishment and a new interior, then runs fine without any damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restored' rearranges SAAB into ASAB; 'interior' takes E from the middle of 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something completely parched, with no water left at all, like old bleached skeleton remains.

clue.text: Magistrate carrying case of evidence gets military vehicle

indicators.note: one piece carrying another holds it within itself

parts.note: JP is a Justice of the Peace, a lay magistrate in Britain

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A magistrate arrives with a box of evidence in an army truck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal here, but 'case of' means the outside letters, which the magistrate abbreviation is 'carrying' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The four-wheel-drive utility car was developed for the US Army in World War II.

clue.text: Agreed clear-cut points caught by journalist

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: to clear a defendant is to acquit them
E and S are compass points, east and south
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A clear-cut case: the points were caught by the reporter, who agreed.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'clear-cut' must be split: 'clear' is the verb to find not guilty, and 'cut' docks its last letter. 'by' just means beside.
explanation.definitionFit: Going along with something without protest means consenting or complying.

clue.text: Academic's an ethicist primarily, disrespecting all that's sacred

parts.note: a prof (professor) is an academic, the 's being 'is' and so a link

indicators.note: primarily, meaning in the first place, picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A professor who studies ethics is accused of irreverence toward holy things.
explanation.definitionFit: Irreverent language or conduct toward religion or holy matters is called blasphemous or impious.

clue.text: Sure complication follows half of orthopedic foot treatments

indicators.note: the rearranged piece follows, coming after the other
half of the word takes five of its ten letters, here the back half
a complication muddles things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complication will surely follow half of all bone surgeries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' takes PEDIC, the second half of 'orthopedic'; 'complication' rearranges SURE as URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic care of toenails and feet, as at a salon, are chiropody-style beauty sessions.

clue.text: Puts child to bed and has a good meal

definitions.meaning: settling a child under the covers by folding the sheets in
eating heartily, a British informal sense

explanation.surface: A parent settles the children for the night and then sits down to a hearty dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Two phrasal-verb senses: folding bedclothes snugly round someone, and informally eating eagerly.

clue.text: Be kind when I cry terribly at end of play

indicators.note: these pieces go at the end of the other one

parts.note: a play is a theatrical show
I, said by the speaker, is me

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A playgoer asks for gentleness as they weep at the end of the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges CRY into RCY.
explanation.definitionFit: To spare someone or forgive them is to act with compassion and clemency.

clue.text: Doctor keeps providing iron and partner disagrees

indicators.note: one piece keeping others holds them inside

parts.note: providing means if, on condition that
FE is the chemical symbol for iron
in bridge, South (S) is the partner of North

explanation.surface: A doctor hands out iron supplements and their spouse objects.
explanation.walkthrough: S as 'partner' comes from bridge, where North and South play as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a different opinion is to dissent or be at odds with someone.

clue.text: Stay loyal

definitions.meaning: to stem a flow, especially of blood, a verb spelt either way
steadfast and faithful to a cause

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stop bleeding; as an adjective it means committed and dependable.

clue.text: Reject call quite regularly coming in

indicators.note: letters coming in enter the middle of another word

parts.note: to call out is to shout

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone turns away a phone call that comes in fairly often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'quite', and 'coming in' puts them inside the word for call, just after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude or bar something is to refuse it entry, close the door on it.

clue.text: Fantastic laser playing over old city

indicators.note: one piece over another covers it, enclosing it
playing letters are moved around, so they are rearranged

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A laser show plays across the ruins of an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' scrambles 'laser', and 'over' has that scramble cover the ancient Mesopotamian city by enclosing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizarre and dreamlike, like the art movement, means unreal or fantastical.

clue.text: Used to do hair with firm/medium brush initially

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A hairdresser asks whether to use a firm or medium-bristled brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed grooming tool is the implement one runs through hair to tidy it.

clue.text: Time and time again fell short framing slogan

indicators.note: framing pieces surround the others
short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a fell is an upland moor in northern England
a second T for time

explanation.surface: Repeatedly falling short of a catchphrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' is not the past of fall but a northern English moor; 'short' cuts MOOR to MOO, which frames TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase summing up a principle or belief is a maxim or watchword.

clue.text: Husband has admirer thrown out by valet

indicators.note: something thrown out is disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a manservant or valet is a 'man', as in Jeeves being Bertie Wooster's man

explanation.surface: A husband has his wife's admirer ejected by the servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse who is male, someone wed, is literally a man with a wife.

clue.text: Loads of space inside to have a doze

indicators.note: one piece inside another sits within it

parts.note: to nod or nod off is to doze
an en is a printing space, half an em

explanation.surface: There is plenty of room inside for a nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'en' is the printers' measure of space.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, an unlimited amount means a great many, lots.

clue.text: Sun's shown up endless dirt and waste on top of water

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read bottom to top
endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: muck is dirt

explanation.surface: Sunlight reveals grime and rubbish floating on a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims MUCK to MUC, which 'shown up' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth or film of impurities floating on a liquid is the classic sense of this word.

clue.text: Reserve judgment in conversation about rite going ahead

indicators.note: going ahead puts this piece in front of the other
about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged
words in conversation are spoken, so we want a sound-alike spelling

parts.note: good judgment is sense

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their opinion to themselves while discussing a ceremony that is going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' scrambles 'rite'; 'going ahead' puts that first; 'in conversation' means the word for judgment is only heard, so its spelling changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a personal quality is restraint, a disinclination to speak openly.

clue.text: Make a sculpture with victory in mind

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to mind is to care, be concerned
V is for victory, as in the V sign

explanation.surface: An artist sculpts with a triumph in mind, perhaps a war memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaping wood or stone by cutting is how a sculptor fashions a figure.

clue.text: Woman turned back crossing hill in downpour

indicators.note: one piece crossing another spans it, holding it in the middle
turned back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: Ms is the title for a woman
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A woman hiking over a hill turns back when caught in heavy rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses the title for a woman, and 'crossing' has it straddle the Dartmoor-style hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent weather event with heavy rain and wind is a tempest bringing a deluge.

clue.text: Took time off and gardened outside, working daily

indicators.note: one piece outside another wraps around it

parts.note: to hoe is to garden, weeding the soil

indicators.note: letters working are being worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who weeded outdoors every day finally took a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' scrambles 'daily', and 'outside' has the gardening verb's past tense wrap around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending a vacation means taking a break away from work, in British usage.
